source_text: Nihil sine origine nisi deus solus. quae quantum praecedit in statu omnium rerum, tantum praecedat necesse est etiam in retractatu earum, ut constare de statu possit, quia nec habeas dispicere quid quale sit, nisi certus an sit, cum cognoueris unde sit. et ideo ex opusculi ordine ad hanc materiam deuolutus apostoli quoque Pauli originem a Marcione desidero, nouus aliqui discipulus nec ullius alterius auditor, qui nihil interim credam nisi nihil temere credendum, temere porro credi quodcumque sine originis agnitione credetur, quique dignissime ad sollicitudinem redigam istam inquisitionem, cum is mihi adfirmatur apostolus, quem in albo apostolorum apud euangelium non deprehendo. denique audiens postea eum a domino adlectum iam in caelis quiescente, quasi improuidentiam existimo, si non ante sciit illum sibi necessarium Christus, sed iam ordinato officio apostolatus et in sua opera dimisso ex incursu, non ex prospectu adiciendum existimauit, necessitate, ut ita dixerim, non uoluntate. quamobrem, Pontice nauclere, si numquam furtiuas merces uel inlicitas in acatos tuas recepisti, si numquam omnino onus auertisti uel adulterasti, +cautior utique et fidelior in dei rebus edas uelim nobis, quo symbolo susceperis apostolum Paulum, quis illum tituli charactere percusserit, quis transmiserit tibi, quis imposuerit, ut possis eum constanter exponere. ne illius probetur, qui omnia apostolatus eius instrumenta protulit, \'ipse se\', inquit, \'apostolum est professus, et quidem non ab hominibus nec per hominem, sed per legum Christum\'. plane profiteri potest semetipsum quis, uerum professio eius alterius auctoritate conficitur. alius scribit alius subscribit, alius obsignat alius actis refert. nemo sibi et professor et testis est. praeter haec utique legisti multos uenturos, qui dicant: ego sum Christus. si est qui se Christum mentiatur, quanto magis qui se apostolum praedicet Christi? adhuc ego in persona discipuli et inquisitoris conuersor, ut iam hinc et fidem tuam obtundam, qui unde eam probes non habes, et impudentiam suffundam, qui uindicas et unde possis uindicare non recipis. sit Christus, sit et apostolus nunc alterius, dum non probantur nisi de instrumento creatoris. nam mihi Paulum etiam Genesis olim repromisit. inter illas enim figuras et propheticas super filios suos benedictiones Iacob, cum ad Beniamin direxisset: Beniamin, inquit, lupus rapax; ad matutinum comedet adhuc et ad uesperam dabit escam. ex tribu enim Beniamin oriturum Paulum prouidebat, lupum rapacem ad matutinum comedentem, id est prima aetate uastaturum pecora domini ut persecutorem ecclesiaium, dehinc ad uesperam escam daturum, id est deuergente iam aetate oues Christi educaturum ut doctorem nationum. nam et Saulis primo asperitas insectationis erga Dauid, dehinc paenitentia et satisfactio, bona pro malis recipientis, non aliud portendebat quam Paulum in Saule secundum tribus et legum in Dauid secundum uirginis censum. haec figurarum sacramenta si tibi displicent, certe Acta Apostolorum hunc mihi ordinem Pauli tradiderunt, a te quoque non negandum. inde apostolum ostendo persecutorem non ab hominibus neque per hominem, inde et ipsi credere inducor, inde te a defensione eius expello nec timeo dicentem: tu ergo negas apostolum Paulum? non blasphemo quem tueor. nego, ut te probare compellam; nego, ut meum esse conuincam. aut, si ad nostram fidem spectas, recipe quae eam faciunt; si ad tuam prouocas, ede quae eam praestruunt. aut proba esse quae credis aut, si non probas, quomodo credis? aut qualis es aduersus eum credens, a quo solo probatur esse quod credis? habe nunc et apostolum de meo sicut et Christum, quam meum apostolum quam et Christum: isdem et hic dimicabimus lineis, in ipso gradu prouocabimus praescriptionis, oportere scilicet et apostolum, qui creatoris negetur immo et aduersus creatorem proferatur, nihil docere, nihil sapere, nihil uelle secundum creatorem, et inprimis tanta constantia alium deum edicere, quanta a lege creatoris abrupit. neque enim uerisimile est, ut auertens a Iudaismo non pariter ostenderet, in cuius dei fidem auerteret, quia nemo transire posset a creatore nesciens, ad quem transeundum sibi esset. siue enim Christus iam alium deum reuelauerat, sequebatur etiam apostoli testatio, uel ne non eius dei apostolus haberetur, quem Christus reuelauerat, et quia non licebat abscondi ab apostolo qui iam reuelatus fuisset a Christo; siue nihil tale de deo Christus reuelauerat, [at] tanto magis ab apostolo debuerat reuelari qui iam non posset ab alio, non credendus sine dubio, si nec ab apostolo reuelatus. quod idcirco praestruximus, ut iam hinc profiteamur nos proinde probaturos nullum alium deum ab apostolo circumlatum, sicut probauimus nec a Christo, ex ipsis utique epistolis Pauli, quas proinde mutilatas etiam de numero forma iam haeretici euangelii praeiudicasse debebit.
pass_a_gloss: Nothing is without origin except God alone. As much as He precedes in the state of all things, so much must He also precede in the investigation of them, so that it may be established about the state, because you cannot know what something is like unless you are certain that it exists, when you have learned where it is from. And therefore, following the order of this work, I, a new disciple and not a listener to anyone else, who meanwhile do not believe anything unless it is not to be believed rashly, and rashly, moreover, everything that is believed without knowledge of its origin is believed, and who most worthily reduce this investigation to anxiety, when that apostle is affirmed to me, whom I do not find in the list of apostles in the Gospel. Finally, hearing afterwards that he was called by the Lord, already resting in heaven, I consider it as a lack of foresight, if Christ did not know beforehand that he was necessary to Him, but, with the office of apostleship already established and sent out in His work from a sudden attack, not from foresight, He considered him to be added out of necessity, so to speak, not by will. Wherefore, Ponticus, if you have never received stolen or illicit goods in your ships, if you have never altogether avoided or adulterated a cargo, I wish you to be more cautious and faithful in the things of God, and to tell us by what symbol you have received the apostle Paul, who has struck him with the character of his title, who has transmitted him to you, who has imposed him, so that you can constantly expound him. Lest it be proven that he, who has brought forth all the instruments of his apostleship, says 'he himself is an apostle, and indeed not from men nor through a man, but through Christ'. Anyone can certainly profess himself, but his profession is confirmed by the authority of another. One person writes, another subscribes, another seals, another reports in the acts. No one is both a professor and a witness for himself. Besides these things, you have certainly read that many will come, who will say: 'I am Christ'. If there is someone who lies that he is Christ, how much more so someone who preaches that he is an apostle of Christ? I still speak in the person of a disciple and inquirer, so that from now on I may both blunt your faith, which you do not have from where you can prove it, and pour out shame on your impudence, which you vindicate and from where you can vindicate it you do not receive. Let Christ exist, let another apostle exist now, as long as they are not proven except from the instrument of the Creator. For Paul was also promised to me by Genesis long ago. For among those figures and prophetic blessings of the sons of Jacob, when he had directed himself to Benjamin, he said: 'Benjamin, a rapacious wolf; in the morning he will eat, and in the evening he will give food'. For from the tribe of Benjamin, he was providing for Paul to arise, a rapacious wolf eating in the morning, that is, in his early age devastating the flocks of the Lord as a persecutor of the churches, and then in the evening giving food, that is, with his age already turning, he will educate the sheep of Christ as a teacher of the nations. For also the asperity of Saul's persecution towards David at first, and then his repentance and satisfaction, receiving good for evil, did not portend anything other than Paul in Saul, according to the tribes and the law in David, according to the census of the virgin. If these sacraments of the figures do not please you, certainly the Acts of the Apostles have handed down this order of Paul to me, which you also cannot deny. From there I show the apostle as a persecutor not from men nor through a man, from there I also induce you to believe, from there I drive you away from his defense, and I do not fear your saying: 'So you deny the apostle Paul?' I do not blaspheme whom I defend. I deny, so that I may compel you to prove; I deny, so that I may convince that he is mine. Or, if you look to our faith, receive what makes it; if you provoke to yours, bring forth what establishes it. Or prove that what you believe exists, or, if you do not prove, how do you believe? Or what kind of person are you, believing in him, by whom alone what you believe is proven to exist? Have now both the apostle from me, just as Christ, whom I consider my apostle, just as Christ: we will fight with the same lines, we will provoke the prescription in the same degree, namely, that the apostle, who is denied by the Creator, or even brought forth against the Creator, teaches nothing, knows nothing, wills nothing according to the Creator, and, above all, proclaims another God with as much constancy as he has torn away from the law of the Creator. For it is not likely that, turning away from Judaism, he would not equally show in whose God's faith he was turning away, because no one can pass from the Creator without knowing to whom he is passing. For either Christ had already revealed another God, and the apostle's testimony followed, or, so that he would not be considered an apostle of another God, whom Christ had revealed, and because it was not permitted to hide from the apostle what had already been revealed by Christ; or, if Christ had not revealed such a thing about God, all the more so the apostle ought to have revealed it, who could no longer be believed without doubt, if he had not been revealed by the apostle. We have established this, so that from now on we may profess that we will prove that no other God is being introduced by the apostle, just as we have proven that none is introduced by Christ, certainly from Paul's own letters, which, in the same way, must be considered mutilated, and even from the number and form of the heretic's Gospel, must have prejudged.

pass_b_english: Nothing has an origin except God alone. Just as he precedes all things in their very existence, so must he also precede our investigation of them. We cannot determine what something is like unless we are first certain that it exists, and we cannot know that until we have learned where it came from. That is why, following the order of this treatise, I turn to the question of the apostle Paul's origin — a question Marcion cannot answer. I am a new disciple, beholden to no other master. I believe nothing that ought not to be believed rashly; indeed, anything believed without knowledge of its origin is believed rashly. I take up this inquiry with the seriousness it deserves, because Paul is presented to me as an apostle whom I simply do not find in the Gospel's list of apostles. Later I hear he was called by the Lord, already enthroned in heaven. That strikes me as a failure of foresight: if Christ did not know beforehand that he needed Paul, then with the apostolic office already established and dispatched, he added Paul only as an afterthought — a sudden raid, not a planned reinforcement — out of necessity, so to speak, not by choice.

So, Ponticus, captain of your own ship: if you have never taken stolen or contraband cargo aboard, if you have never shorted or adulterated a load, then be at least as careful and faithful in the things of God. Tell us by what token you received the apostle Paul — who branded him with his title, who handed him over to you, who imposed him on you — so that you can give a consistent account of him. Do not let it be proved that the man who produced all the credentials of his own apostleship is the one who says, 'I am an apostle — not from men nor through a man, but through Jesus Christ' (Gal 1:1). Anyone can profess himself, but a profession is confirmed only by another's authority. One writes, another subscribes, another seals, another enters it in the record. No one is both professor and witness for himself. Besides, you have read that many will come saying, 'I am the Christ' (Matt 24:5). If someone can lie and claim to be Christ, how much more will someone lie and claim to be an apostle of Christ?

I am still speaking as a disciple and an examiner. My aim is to blunt your faith — since you have no source from which to prove it — and to shame your impudence, since you defend a claim you cannot substantiate. Let Christ be; let there be another apostle for now — provided they are not authenticated except from the Creator's own documents. For Genesis promised Paul to me long ago. Among those prophetic figures and blessings Jacob pronounced over his sons, when he turned to Benjamin he said: 'Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the spoil' (Gen 49:27). From the tribe of Benjamin, Jacob foresaw Paul rising — a ravenous wolf devouring in the morning, that is, in his youth ravaging the Lord's flocks as a persecutor of the churches; then in the evening distributing food, that is, in his later years feeding Christ's sheep as a teacher of the nations. Saul's early ferocity against David, followed by repentance and restitution — receiving good for evil — foreshadowed nothing other than Paul in Saul, of the tribe of Benjamin and under the Law, and David according to the virgin's lineage.

If these sacramental figures displease you, the Acts of the Apostles have handed down this same sequence for Paul, and you cannot deny it. From Acts I show the apostle as a persecutor — not from men nor through a man (Gal 1:1); from Acts I bring you to believe; from Acts I drive you from his defense. I do not fear your retort: 'So you deny the apostle Paul?' I do not blaspheme the one I defend. I deny him precisely to force you to prove him; I deny him to demonstrate that he belongs to me. If you look to our faith, accept the evidence that establishes it; if you challenge us to yours, produce the evidence that constitutes it. Either prove that what you believe exists, or if you cannot prove it, how do you believe? What kind of believer are you, trusting a man by whom alone the object of your faith is proven to exist? You now have the apostle from my side, just as you have Christ — whom I claim as my apostle no less than my Christ. We will fight on the same lines; we will press the prescription at the same point: that an apostle who is repudiated by the Creator, or rather deployed against the Creator, teaches nothing, knows nothing, wills nothing according to the Creator, and above all proclaims another god with the same constancy with which he tore himself from the Creator's Law. It is not plausible that, turning from Judaism, he would not equally declare whose God he was turning to — because no one can pass from the Creator without knowing to whom he is passing. Either Christ had already revealed another God, and the apostle's testimony followed — otherwise he would not be the apostle of the God Christ revealed, and what Christ had revealed could not be hidden from the apostle — or Christ revealed nothing of the sort about God, in which case the apostle was all the more obliged to reveal it, since he could no longer be believed without doubt if the revelation did not come through him. We have laid this groundwork so that from now on we may declare our intention to prove that no other God is being smuggled in by the apostle, just as we have proven none is smuggled in by Christ — and we will do it from Paul's own letters, which the heretic's Gospel, in its very number and form, has already prejudged as mutilated.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause translation, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that preserves all nuances, including the complex theological arguments regarding the apostle's origin and the relationship between the Creator and the revealed God. Scripture citations in Pass B (Gal 1:1, Matt 24:5, Gen 49:27) correctly identify the content of the Latin allusions/quotes. The title 'Investigating Paul's Origin' correctly names the thought of the chapter.
